newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran sentences woman to death on morals charges.
newsitem.headline: Iran sentences woman to death on morals charges.

text.p: Iran's Supreme Court has upheld the death sentence against an Iranian woman for acting as a procuress for a gang convicted of economic sabotage and spying, a newspaper said on Tuesday.

The daily Iran said Sheyda Khorramzadeh Esfahani had been convicted of helping the gang by organising "corrupt gatherings" with prostitutes, alcohol, drugs, music and dance "to establish immoral contacts with people in various government bodies".
It was the first report of the woman's conviction, apparently passed by a closed Islamic court. Trials on morals charges in Iran are often held behind closed doors.

The Supreme Court also upheld death sentences against three men, convicted of leading the network of 150 members involved in economic fraud during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war and contacts with "foreigners" and opposition groups, the newspaper added.

It did not say which foreign powers they had been in contact with but earlier reports said the three were charged at their trial which began in January 1996 of spying for Israel and the United States Central Intelligence service (CIA).

The men, two businessmen and a former air force officer, were sentenced to death in July after being convicted of setting up several companies as fronts for their operations which included defrauding state banks of large sums, bribing officials and helping people leave Iran illegally.
